question: Should OpenClaw accept this package-update contract: preserve local packaged `dist` edits by default, optionally replay them with `--reapply-local-overrides`, and fail closed on post-cutover content-inventory drift except for the exact legacy allowlist?
rationale: The code path changes installed package contents and package integrity validation, so correctness alone does not settle the intended compatibility and security boundary for existing update workflows.

options.title: Finish package-owner review
options.body: Keep the PR in draft until the package/update owner confirms the local override recovery contract, legacy content-inventory allowlist, and replay safety model.

options.title: Accept the current contract
options.body: Merge as-is if maintainers explicitly accept the new flag, preserve-only default, and strict post-cutover package validation as the desired upgrade boundary.

options.title: Split or narrow the change
options.body: Pause this PR and split content-inventory hardening from local override recovery if the replay or legacy-compatibility direction is too broad.

recommendation.title: Finish package-owner review
recommendation.body: Keep the PR in draft until the package/update owner confirms the local override recovery contract, legacy content-inventory allowlist, and replay safety model.
